4th Period.workingNow: Working out the states your first mod mechanic needs, and what switches between them.
4th Period.weeklyDeliverable: One design document in your portfolio repo bringing together your mechanics, dynamics, aesthetic and state map — plus your ROLLER game embedded and playable on your portfolio site — pushed by Sunday night.
4th Period.smartGoal: I can map the states of one mechanic so that I know exactly what I have to build first.
4th Period.contentStandard: CA CS Standards 6-8.AP.10 — Use flowcharts and/or pseudocode to design solutions to complex problems.
4th Period.eldStandard: ELD.PI.6-8.6 — Reading closely and explaining how meaning is conveyed explicitly and implicitly through language.
agenda: I do: which states does your mechanic need? (8 min)
We do: map one mod mechanic together (6 min)
You do: write your state map (10 min)
4th Period.connections: Your MDA design says what your mod should feel like. Today you take the one mechanic you care most about and break it into states — the same pattern the 6th and 7th graders are learning this week. This is the last piece your design document needs. Tomorrow you assemble the whole thing.

6th Period.workingNow: Adding a third state to your diagram and checking which way each arrow points.
6th Period.weeklyDeliverable: Your completed Game Plan document — two mechanics each with a number, five states, how the mechanics connect to the states, and your first level described — typed and turned in by Sunday night.
6th Period.smartGoal: I can add a third state to my diagram so that my thing can move through a cycle instead of just flipping back and forth.
6th Period.contentStandard: CA CS Standards 6-8.AP.10 — Use flowcharts and/or pseudocode to design solutions to complex problems.
6th Period.eldStandard: ELD.PI.6-8.6 — Reading closely and explaining how meaning is conveyed explicitly and implicitly through language.
agenda: Overview: adding a third state (2 min)
I do: the traffic light, three states (8 min)
We do: why these arrows only go one way (6 min)
You do: add a third state to your diagram (10 min)
Exit Ticket: your third state (2 min)
6th Period.connections: Two states can only flip back and forth. Three states can go in a circle — that is how a traffic light works, and it is why arrows have a direction. Tomorrow you push it to five states and hunt for dead ends.
